item.title: 1988: Hall of Fame Announces Women in Baseball Permanent Display
item.description: The National Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum announces the inauguration of Women in Baseball, a permanent display to honor the entire All-American Girls Professional Baseball League rather than any individual figure. The AAGPBL began play in 1943 and lasted a dozen years, giving more than 500 women an opportunity that had never existed before. Photo: Florida Memory (Public domain).

item.title: 2023: Winnipeg Goldeyes Ballpark Renamed Blue Cross Park
item.description: Following the Rogers Communications acquisition of Shaw Communications, the Winnipeg Goldeyes announced a new 10-year naming rights partnership with Manitoba Blue Cross on November 8, 2023, with the ballpark being renamed Blue Cross Park.

item.title: 2021: Dodgers Announce 2021 Dodger Holiday Festival Event
item.description: On November 8, 2021, the Dodgers announced the "2021 Dodger Holiday Festival" event. Photo: Ken Lund from Reno, Nevada, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2017: LeVangie Replaces Carl Willis as Boston Pitching Coach
item.description: LeVangie replaced Carl Willis as Boston pitching coach on November 8, 2017, on the staff of new manager Alex Cora.

item.title: 2010: Morgan Won't Return to ESPN Sunday Night Baseball for 2011
item.description: In the wake of Morgan taking an official role with the Cincinnati Reds as a "special adviser to baseball operations", it was announced on November 8, 2010, that Morgan would not be returning for the 2011 season as an announcer on ESPN Sunday Night Baseball. Photo: Cincinnati Reds (Public domain).

item.title: 1996: Bruce Bochy Named NL Manager of the Year, Edging Alou, LaRussa
item.description: Bruce Bochy who led the San Diego Padres to their first post season appearance since the 1984 World Series was named National League Manager of the year, just edging out the Montreal Expos' Felipe Alou and the St. Louis Cardinals' Tony LaRussa for the honor.

item.title: 1990: Darryl Strawberry Signs 5-Year Contract With Dodgers
item.description: After 8 up and down years with The New York Mets, Darryl Strawberry signs a 5-year contract with The Los Angeles Dodgers. Photo: slgckgc (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1987: Korakuen Stadium Closes, Demolition Begins Next Day
item.description: Korakuen Stadium closed on November 8, 1987, and demolition began the next day, which was completed in February 1988. Photo: Wikimedia Commons (Attribution).

item.title: 1984: 54 Players Granted Free Agency, Including Eckersley and Fingers
item.description: The ranks of players granted free agency swells by 54 names today—and some of them are the biggest in baseball: future Hall of Famers Dennis Eckersley, Rollie Fingers, Tony Pérez and Bruce Sutter; the NL's Cy Young Award-winner, Rick Sutcliffe; and still-elite players like Dave Kingman, Fred Lynn, Rick Reuschel and André Thornton. Photo: Rubenstein (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1979: Yankees Sign Bob Watson, 33, and Rudy May, 35
item.description: The Yankees sign two top-ranked veterans who were granted free agency on November 1: first baseman Bob Watson, 33, formerly of the Boston Red Sox, and left-handed hurler and ex-Yankee Rudy May, 35, formerly of the Montreal Expos. In 1980, Watson will bat .307 in 130 games, and the versatile May will win 15 of 20 decisions and lead the American League in earned run average (2.46).

item.title: 1977: Bucky Harris, American Baseball Player and Manager
item.description: Bucky Harris, American baseball player and manager (born 1896) Photo: National Photo Company Collection (Public domain).

item.title: 1974: Padres Trade Cito Gaston to Braves for Danny Frisella
item.description: The San Diego Padres trade outfielder Cito Gaston to the Braves for pitcher Danny Frisella. Gaston is an "original Padre," selected by San Diego (from Atlanta) in the 1968 NL expansion draft. Photo: Mikerussell at en.wikipedia (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1973: Bob Chipman, 55, Pitcher for Brooklyn, Chicago and Boston
item.description: Bob Chipman, 55, pitcher who spent all or part of 12 years in the National League (1941–1952) with Brooklyn, Chicago and Boston, appearing in 293 games.

item.title: 1972: Cardinals Bring Tim McCarver Back to St. Louis
item.description: The St. Louis Cardinals bring catcher Tim McCarver back to St. Louis, sending young outfielder Jorge Roque to the Montreal Expos in exchange. Photo: Bret Linford Delaywaves (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1967: Mets Acquire Art Shamsky From Reds for Bob Johnson
item.description: The New York Mets acquire outfielder Art Shamsky from the Cincinnati Reds for utility infielder Bob "Rocky" Johnson. Shamsky will be a key figure on the 1969 "Miracle Mets", batting .300 in 100 regular-season games and .538 in the Mets' 1969 NLCS sweep. Photo: Flcikr user slgckgc (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1966: Frank Robinson Wins AL MVP, First in Both Leagues
item.description: Frank Robinson of the world-champion Baltimore Orioles wins the American League Most Valuable Player Award, becoming the first man to gain MVP recognition by the BBWAA in each major league; he had won the NL award in 1961. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1955: Senators Send Mickey Vernon, Bob Porterfield to Red Sox
item.description: In a nine-player transaction, the Washington Senators send pitchers Bob Porterfield and Johnny Schmitz, first baseman Mickey Vernon and outfielder Tom Umphlett to the Boston Red Sox in exchange for pitchers Dick Brodowski, Tex Clevenger and minor-leader Al Curtis, and outfielders Neil Chrisley and Karl Olson. Veterans Porterfield and Vernon are former All-Stars.

item.title: 1954: Phillies Buy Connie Mack Stadium From Arnold Johnson
item.description: R. R. M. Carpenter Jr., owner of Philadelphia's lone surviving MLB team, the Phillies, tells the press he will reluctantly purchase Connie Mack Stadium from Arnold Johnson, new owner of the soon-to-be-called Kansas City Athletics. The Phillies have shared the ballpark, built in 1909, as tenants of the Athletics since 1938, and have no other suitable place to play until a modern stadium can be built. Photo: ACME Newspictures (Public domain).

item.title: 1954: Arnold Johnson Moves Athletics to Kansas City, Sells Yankee Stadium
item.description: After he purchased the Philadelphia Athletics and transferred the franchise to Kansas City on November 8, 1954, Johnson sold Yankee Stadium to John W. Photo: Severin St. Martin (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1951: Yogi Berra, 26, Wins First of Three AL MVP Awards
item.description: Campanella's opposite number in The Bronx, Yogi Berra, wins the first of his three American League Most Valuable Player Awards. Cooperstown-bound Berra, 26, batted .294 (27 homers, 88 runs batted in) for the AL champion New York Yankees in 1951. In the balloting, he defeats pitcher Ned Garver by 27 points. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1940: Clark Griffith Invests $130,000 to Light Senators' Ballpark
item.description: Clark Griffith, patriarch of the Washington Senators and known as an outspoken opponent of night baseball, changes course and announces that he's investing $130,000 to equip his club's home ballpark with lights. The Senators plan to host seven night contests in 1941. Photo: National Photo Company Collection (Public domain).

item.title: 1912: Cupid Childs, 45, Former Second Baseman
item.description: Cupid Childs, 45, second baseman for the Spiders/Orphans/Stars/Perfectos/Quakers from 1888 to 1901, a .306 career hitter with 1214 hits, who topped the American Association in doubles (1890) and the National League in runs (1892), while ranking third all-time in walks (991) upon retirement. Photo: Issued by: Goodwin & Company (Public domain).

item.title: 1894: King Kelly, 36, Hall of Fame Catcher and Outfielder
item.description: King Kelly, 36, Hall of Fame catcher and right fielder for the Chicago and Boston National League teams, known as a fiery and alert competitor that developed the hit-and-run and caused numerous refinements of sport's rules upon his exploitation of loopholes, who batted .308 lifetime with two batting titles, led the league in runs and doubles three times each, starred on five Chicago champion teams, and managed… Photo: Goodwin & Company (Public domain).
